title: Rabbi Shimon HaShiloni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: One precious homily of his survives in [Pesachim 118a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.118a). When Nebuchadnezzar cast Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah into the fiery furnace, Yurkemi, the prince of hail, stood before the Holy One, blessed be He, etc. At that moment Gabriel began and said, “And the truth of the Lord.” Rabbi Natan says: “And the truth of the Lord is forever”—the fish in the sea said it. This suggests that he was a tanna, since Rabbi Natan disagrees with him. The later phrase “as Rav Huna said” comes from the redactors of the Gemara.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The printed קיח. conventionally gives 118a; the earlier English omitted the a/b side. Hyman abbreviates the homily with etc.; no omitted requests or answers are supplied. The identification as a tanna and the explanation of the Rav Huna phrase are Hyman’s source-critical argument, not an independently established chronology or redactional attribution. Yurkemi follows the supplied spelling יורקמי. No named passage or edition was checked in the earlier preparation; the subsequent title comparison is noted below.

The William Davidson Hebrew text explicitly titles Shimon HaShiloni at Pesachim 118a:21. The continuation at 118b:1–2 explicitly titles Natan and Huna in the quoted discussion. This checks those title forms, without independently establishing Hyman’s chronology or redactional inference.
